comments.author: @massimocolasanti7295
comments.text: I lived in Sweden 🇸🇪 for 18 years; I speak Swedish and love the country 🇸🇪... but Sweden isn't the paradise people make it out to be. Sweden always has the same little lakes, cottages, farms, and towns: everything is exactly the same! Swedes are racist towards us Italians 🇮🇹. There is an underlying contempt for us everywhere... And the icing on the cake...: Nobles and the wealthy have greater inheritance rights than the common people, who count for nothing. University admissions are... a scam: only the children of the rich get into prestigious degree programs—kids whose parents have carefully curated their academic records since elementary school to ensure they come out on top. The result? University-educated fools everywhere, while intelligent poor people are stuck working in factories. 80% of Swedes live under a lifetime residency right that requires monthly payments; they are essentially renting from a private bank that holds the keys and can enter whenever it wants (*bostadsrätt*). Taxes on detached houses are sky-high. The Swedish healthcare system is decentralized... leading to depressing logistical issues and a reliance on connections to get surgery on time and by the best doctors; many doctors are ill-prepared, and a lot of them are 'shady' foreigners. There is a lot of corruption... well-hidden! The big cities look... Arab and dangerous! Oh... I almost forgot! On Friday afternoons, Saturdays, and Sundays, you run into people who—after queuing at *Systembolaget* (the state alcohol monopoly)—go home to spend three days drunk... and... that applies to almost all Swedes: even the police look wasted! Sweden 🇸🇪, like Finland 🇫🇮 and Norway 🇧🇻, is among the happiest countries in the world (according to panels of experts with a socio-communist, materialist bent)... yet it is a place where, to find a sense of joy, people seek to forget everything in an alcohol-induced oblivion. An Italian friend of mine 🇮🇹, a professor of psychiatry, described the Swedes 🇸🇪 as: "a people of scrubbed-up former peasants living in a state of materialist hedonism." Perhaps that is the right definition for the Swedish people... a nation that lectures everyone else on hygiene, even though just a century ago, the parish priest had to force the faithful to bathe in a large tub of hot water in the village square—and only at Easter! It is a place where apartment buildings have communal washing machines that serve as sources of infection for the residents... and where garbage, tossed down chutes in the stairwells, ends up in a room on the ground floor of the building

comments.author: @christiansvensson3571
comments.text: Sweden is a fantastic country with a lot to offer international tourists, to see and experience. Recommended! Varied Swedish music and Swedish artists such as accordion music, rock carvings, ancient remains, archipelagos with islands, nature reserves, amusement parks, good Swedish home cooking such as varied food and much more. Some old famous Swedish musicians and artists, but who are no longer alive, are Povel Ramel, Thore Skogman, Stefan Demert, Fredrik Åkerström and Cornelis Vreeswijk and many more. But personally, I myself prefer listening to Balochi music the most, as well as international world music with various artists in different languages more than Swedish and English music. Greetings from Christian Svensson, Sweden. PS. I love and like Balochi music 100 % a lot, as a Swedish person, more than ever. This music has such pleasant rhythms, melodies and beats. There is nothing as 100% very great recommendable as Balochi music. Balochi music has a great and rich variety of different mixed instruments such as different flutes and string instruments, known for its traditional culture with lovely sounds and beautiful music styles and genres. Recommended 100 % for everyone, worldwide! For me too. Love music and world music in different languages! The melodies and rhythms of Balochi music really make me smile and dig. 👋😊💕💕👋😀❤❤👌☺👍

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
